key_insight: Reactive sputtering can produce epitaxial Mn4N thin films with strong perpendicular magnetic anisotropy on MgO(100), making the material viable for spin-orbitronic device use.
engineering_relevance: This work points to a scalable, rare-earth-free route for current-driven magnetic memory and switching devices with tunable coercivity and efficient spin-orbit torque behavior.
method: Reactive magnetron sputtering of Mn4N on MgO(100) and SrTiO3(100) substrates
Structural, magnetic, and magnetotransport characterization of film quality and anisotropy
Density functional theory calculations to assess strain and interfacial contributions
evidence_signal: The optimized films showed square hysteresis loops, large tunable coercivity, a pronounced anomalous Hall effect, and efficient current-induced switching in Mn4N/Pt bilayers.
watch_item: Perpendicular anisotropy depends not only on epitaxial strain but also on interfacial effects, so performance may be sensitive to substrate and interface control.
paper_title: Optimization of Epitaxial Mn4N Thin Films Grown by Sputtering for Spintronic Applications
